A base with init() and a subclass inheriting that initializer therefore selects init, which fails with "Swift base method has no `func` declaration" at crates/prod-code-mcp/src/replace_inheritance/languages/swift.rs:134. findings.title: Exclude Swift initializers from default method forwarding
evidence: crates/prod-code-mcp/src/pull_push/languages/swift.rs:119-147 recognizes init, names it init, and classifies it as MemberKind::Method; the aggregate base recognized only func declarations.
crates/prod-code-mcp/src/replace_inheritance/execute.rs:93-119 selects all such methods for omitted/empty selections, excluding constructor and C++ special members but not Swift init.
crates/prod-code-mcp/src/replace_inheritance/languages/swift.rs:76-100 generates an initializer separately and then forwards every selected method.
crates/prod-code-mcp/src/replace_inheritance/languages/swift.rs:132-134 requires a func token and returns the exact error for an initializer.

crates/prod-code-mcp/tests/pull_up_literal_preservation/swift_replacement.rs:17-27 invokes transform_swift with an explicit empty method list; its initializer assertions do not exercise public default discovery.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep parsing Swift initializers for declaration-local modifier removal, and exclude Swift init declarations from the default forwarding set, or give initializers a distinct member kind and filter on actual methods. Add a focused public-entry regression for a base with an explicit init and an inheriting subclass, covering both omitted and empty method selections while confirming speak is forwarded.
